meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

meanings.note: in questions: а вдруг...? = and what if...?
А вдруг... = what if. Core Russian adv meaning 'suddenly; all of a sudden' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level?
Suddenly it began to rain.

examples.text: Почему он вдруг сравнялся? Мы шли впереди на десять процентов!
examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level? We were ten percent ahead!

meanings.note: Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.
Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'genius' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This artist is a true genius.

examples.text: Вы гений и выдающийся ум современности!
examples.trans: You are a genius and the greatest mind of our time!

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You have visitors!

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see

examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'бронировать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to reserve', forming an aspectual pair with 'бронировать'.

examples.text: Макс решил забронировать столик на вечер.
examples.trans: Max decided to reserve a table for the evening.

examples.text: Алло, ресторан, я хочу забронировать столик.
examples.trans: Hello, restaurant, I want to reserve a table.

examples.trans: Pelevin is a mysterious writer, nobody has seen him.

meanings.note: Food, goods, or services. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to order', paired with 'заказать'.

examples.text: Ладно, звони в свою пиццу. Заказывай!

meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.trans: As you all know...

examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'вестный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('famous, well-known').

The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'анный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('devoted, loyal').

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
